solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Agent — with assistance — settled debts

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent for a firm
aid is assistance; 'with' adds it on

explanation.surface: A go-between, helped by someone, finally cleared what was owed.
explanation.definitionFit: To have repaid is to have given back borrowed money, which is exactly what settling debts involves.

clue.text: Hand in your notice, or agree to an updated contract?

explanation.walkthrough: The same letters read as one word mean quit, and read with a hyphen mean sign a fresh contract; the question mark flags the split.
explanation.definitionFit: Resigning means formally leaving a post, while re-signing means putting your name to a renewed deal.

clue.text: Saw traveller entering pubs regularly

indicators.note: entering something means going inside it, so one piece sits within the other
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first and third letters
a rover is a wanderer or traveller

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a wanderer frequently going into bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past-tense verb; it is the noun meaning a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, the same as a proverb.

clue.text: Children's game is pretty devoid of content

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: with its contents removed only the shell of the word remains, its outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that a kids' pastime is attractive but empty.
explanation.definitionFit: I-spy is a guessing game in which children name things they can see by their first letter.

clue.text: It's a nasty, concerning, scornful piece of work

indicators.note: something nasty is in a bad, messed-up state, so the preceding letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
re means 'about' or 'concerning', as in letter headings

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a mean-spirited, mocking piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is a literary or dramatic work that ridicules its targets, hence a scornful composition.

clue.text: Cunning adversary removing header from public record

definitions.note: a noun phrase used attributively, standing for the adjective

indicators.note: a header is the top item, which for a down entry is the first letter, and it is taken off

parts.note: arch means knowingly sly or cunning
a rival is an opponent

explanation.surface: A devious enemy is deleting a heading from an official document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunning adversary' reads as one villain, but cunning gives ARCH and the adversary loses its first letter. ARCHIVAL is an adjective, so 'public record' is read as in a phrase like 'public record material'.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives hold historical public records, so archival material belongs to such records.

clue.text: Midwesterner one performing around Washington

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a performer is on stage
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: A person from the Midwest is playing a gig near the US capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington here is the state, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iowan comes from Iowa, a state in the American Midwest.

clue.text: Trainee dismissing the first profitable venture

indicators.note: dismissing the first means sending away the opening letter

parts.note: a learner is someone in training

explanation.surface: An apprentice sacks the top person and starts a lucrative business.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner, as in 'a nice little earner', is something that brings in money.

clue.text: Try physical training, taking in university field event

parts.note: to have a shot is to have a try

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: PT is the standard abbreviation for physical training
U is the usual abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: An encouragement to attempt gym exercises at a university sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The shot put is an athletics throwing contest held in the field rather than on the track.

clue.text: Type of communication requiring great help, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some form of messaging that apparently needs plenty of assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: The telegraph sent messages by electrical signal over wires, an early system of long-distance contact.

clue.text: After courageously observing at first, we run and cringe in fear

indicators.note: 'at first' points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: opening letter
opening letter
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Having bravely watched something, we flee and shrink back in terror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just tells you the first-letter pair comes before WE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to crouch or shrink back out of fright, a near synonym of cringing.

clue.text: In cooking, he employed clarified butter

indicators.note: 'In' says the answer is found inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of cooking, all of he and the start of employed

explanation.surface: A cook reports using clarified butter in his recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run uses the first letter of employed, so the definition sits at the end with no link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghee is the clarified butter used widely in South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Every husband-to-be initially ignored marriage?

indicators.note: ignoring something initially means dropping its first letter

parts.note: every one means all
a fiancé is a man engaged to be married

explanation.surface: A question of whether every engaged man was overlooked at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags marriage in its looser sense of a union between parties rather than a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is a union or alliance, and dynastic marriages were literally alliances between families.

clue.text: Argue violently about evil fighter

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the other piece
violently suggests a wild disturbance, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
ill can mean evil, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: Two people furiously dispute the wickedness of a combatant.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerilla is an irregular fighter in a small independent band.

clue.text: Buglers struggling to grasp a singular style of country music

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold tightly, so the jumbled letters wrap round what follows
struggling suggests something thrashing about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Brass players labouring to master a single kind of rural American music.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluegrass is a form of American country music from Appalachia, played on banjo, fiddle and mandolin.

clue.text: Small dining stools, for example

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
dining is eating

explanation.surface: Little stools for a dining area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small dining stools' reads as one description of furniture; split it after 'dining'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seating means places to sit collectively, and stools are one kind of it.

clue.text: Animal in a large herd, mostly close to sea

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a pack is a herd or group of animals

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is taken

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: A creature among a big herd, near the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American animal related to the llama, kept for its wool.

clue.text: Stick publicity notice on this spot

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement
here means at this place

explanation.surface: An instruction to fix an advertisement poster at this location.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to a surface.

clue.text: West African left from Portugal, perhaps

parts.note: L is the usual abbreviation for left
Portugal is on the Iberian peninsula; 'perhaps' flags it as one example

explanation.surface: Someone from West Africa departed Portugal, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb about departing; it is only the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberian is a native of Liberia, a country on Africa's west coast.

clue.text: Bachelor, far from prudent and impetuous

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees like BA
rash means reckless, the opposite of prudent

explanation.surface: A single man who is reckless and hot-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Brash means bold and hasty, acting without due thought, which is what impetuous means.

clue.text: Introduction to rondeau penned by terrible poet

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed, as if in a pen, by it

parts.note: terrible means very bad

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: opening letter

explanation.surface: The opening of a rondeau, a short French verse form, was written by a dreadful versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a poet, the word used especially for Shakespeare, the Bard of Avon.

clue.text: Inflammation ends in callous: almost unbearably sore

indicators.note: ends in points to the final letter of each of the following words

parts.note: last letter
last letter
last letter
last letter

explanation.surface: A medical note: swelling in hardened skin, very nearly unbearably painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' looks like a deletion signal but is just one of the four words supplying an end letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the edge of the eyelid.

clue.text: A face covering said to be of use

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the answer is how the earlier words are pronounced

parts.note: a veil is a covering for the face

explanation.surface: A mask or veil is claimed to have some practical purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to help or be of benefit, as in 'it will avail you nothing'.

clue.text: Refurbished hotel featuring one new means of direct access

indicators.note: a refurbished building has been done over and rearranged, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
N is the usual abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A renovated hotel now has a fresh, direct entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotline is a dedicated phone line giving immediate contact, as between heads of state.

clue.text: Rupees invested in a fake religious retreat

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a sham is a fake
R is the abbreviation for rupees, the currency of India

explanation.surface: Indian money was poured into a bogus spiritual refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu hermitage or community where people retreat for religious instruction and meditation.

clue.text: Bird sitting next to black dog

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
an eagle is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A bird perches beside a dark-coated hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sitting next to' places the two pieces side by side; the bird comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: The beagle is a small hound breed used for hunting hares.
